name: Herveus Burgidolensis
evidence: No complete English translation exists, but partial translations of his Isaiah commentary exist on The Divine Lamp blog (chapters 1, 35, and 50). These are blog excerpts, not a published edition. The comprehensive Commentarii in Isaiam prophetam remains untranslated.

name: Isidorus Mercator
evidence: The Pseudo-Isidorian Decretals collection as a whole remains untranslated: 3 searches confirmed Hinschius (1863, Latin) is still the only usable edition, and Eric Knibbs (leading Pseudo-Isidore scholar) has published analysis, not translation. However, one text incorporated in the collection, the Donation of Constantine, has published English translations: Mark Edwards, Constantine and Christendom (Liverpool University Press, 2003) and Johannes Fried, Donation of Constantine and Constitutum Constantini (de Gruyter, 2007, with Latin text and English translation). The forged decretals themselves stand untranslated.

name: Carolus Magnus
evidence: Charlemagne's capitularies, letters, and decrees have been translated into English. P.D. King's 'Charlemagne: Translated Sources' (1987) provides comprehensive English translations of capitularies (pp. 202-268) and letters (pp. 269-330). Free online translations also available via The Avalon Project (Yale Law School), Fordham Internet History Sourcebooks, and De Remilitari.org.

name: Sicardus Cremonensis
evidence: 3 searches found no published complete English translation of the Mitrale (Mitralis de officiis). A German translation exists (L. Weinrich, Corpus Christianorum in Translation vol. 9, Brepols) based on the 2008 CCCM 228 critical Latin edition. An English translation of book 1 by John Weretka was reported in progress (PhilEvents, 2019) but no published English edition located. Original in PL 213 and Internet Archive.

name: Rodulfus Trudonis
evidence: 3 searches found no English translation of the Gesta abbatum Trudonensium. The modern critical edition (Paul Tombeur, 2 vols., 2013, Corpus Christianorum Continuatio Mediaevalis, Brepols) is Latin with French apparatus. Not in Translated Texts for Historians (series covers c. 300-800; Rodulfus is 12th century). Latin text at Documenta Catholica Omnia and MGH.

name: Christianus Druthmarus
evidence: 3 searches (as Christian of Stavelot / Christian Druthmar) found no English translation of the Expositio in Matthaeum Evangelistam. Editio princeps by Wimpfeling (Strasburg, 1514); scholars work from Migne PL 106, cols. 1261-1504. English-language scholarship discusses the commentary (e.g., academia.edu studies) but no translation of the text located; not in the Fathers of the Church Matthew commentary volumes (those are Jerome and Hilary).

name: Wilhelmus Hirsaugiensis
evidence: 3 searches found no English translation of William of Hirsau's works: the music treatise (De musica / Musica), the astronomy writings, or the Constitutiones Hirsaugienses (1079 monastic customs). Texts remain in Patrologia Latina 150. Scholarly discussion in English exists (e.g., Brepols article on Aribo's De musica and Abbot William) but no translation located.

name: Algerus Leodiensis
evidence: The two major works stand untranslated: De misericordia et iustitia exists only in Kretzschmar's critical edition (Sigmaringen, 1985, Latin with German commentary), and De sacramento corporis et sanguinis Domini has no located English translation (Erasmus's editions were Latin). However, Alger's preface to De misericordia et iustitia is translated in Somerville and Brasington, Prefaces to Canon Law Books in Latin Christianity, pp. 165-69 (noted in Cambridge's Great Christian Jurists in the Low Countries chapter search result). Bulk of the corpus remains Latin-only.

name: Henricus de Castro Marsiaco
evidence: 3 searches plus a WebFetch found no English translation of Henry of Marcy's writings (De peregrinante civitate Dei, letters on the 1178/1181 anti-Cathar missions). English scholarship discusses him extensively (Alexander Marx on his Third Crusade preaching; a De Gruyter chapter on his influence on Herbert of Clairvaux) but works remain in Patrologia Latina. Checked the Wakefield & Evans 'Heresies of the High Middle Ages' entry at medievalsourcesbibliography.org: Henry is not among the 21 listed authors.

name: Jacobus Caietanus
evidence: 3 searches found no English translation of Stefaneschi's Opus Metricum (three-part hexameter life of Celestine V, united 1319). Editions are Papebroch in Acta Sanctorum (May IV, 436-483) and F.X. Seppelt, Monumenta Coelestiniana (Paderborn, 1921), both Latin; Italian scholarship exists (Filologia mediolatina article) but no English version located.

name: Godefridus Viterbiensis
evidence: 3 searches found no English translation of the Pantheon, Speculum regum, or Memoria seculorum. Latin editions: first print 1559, extracts in Muratori's Rerum Italicarum scriptores vii (1725), MGH. English scholarship exists (Thomas Foerster, Godfrey of Viterbo and his Readers, Ashgate 2015; De Gruyter chapters; a ProQuest dissertation on the Pantheon's transmission) but these are studies, not translations.

name: Richerus S. Remigii
evidence: Richer of Reims' Histories has been translated into English by Justin Lake. Published in 2011 by Dumbarton Oaks Medieval Library (Harvard University Press) in two volumes with facing-page Latin-English text (Books 1-2 in Vol. I, Books 3-4 in Vol. II). This is now the standard English version.

name: Gualterus de Castellione
evidence: Walter of Châtillon's Alexandreis has two English translations: (1) David Townsend's verse translation (University of Pennsylvania Press, 1996) - the first-ever English verse translation and now the standard version; (2) R. Telfryn Pritchard's prose translation (Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies, Toronto, 1986). Both are published.

name: Herbertus Turrium in Sardinia
evidence: 3 searches found no English translation of Herbert of Clairvaux's Liber miraculorum / Liber visionum et miraculorum Clarevallensium. The 2017 Brepols critical edition (CCCM) has Latin text with Italian introduction and notes; a German study edition exists (Kompatscher Gufler, Peter Lang). Not in Cistercian Publications' translated series (Caesarius of Heisterbach and Exordium Magnum are translated; Herbert is not). English scholarship (De Gruyter chapter, ResearchGate 'Herbert of Torres' profile) discusses but does not translate the work.

name: Amulo Lugdunensis
evidence: Amulo's predestination writings ARE translated: Victor Genke and Francis X. Gumerlock, Gottschalk and a Medieval Predestination Controversy: Texts Translated from the Latin (Marquette University Press, Mediaeval Philosophical Texts in Translation 47, 2010) includes Amolo of Lyons' 'Letter to Gottschalk' and 'On Grace and Foreknowledge' in English. A translated Amulo excerpt on relics also appears in the Fordham Medieval Sourcebook. However, his largest work, the Epistola seu Liber contra Judaeos (846, to Charles the Bald), and the Sententiae ex libris Augustini remain untranslated (Latin only, PL 116).

name: Anselmus Lucensis
evidence: The Collectio canonum (bulk of the corpus, 1,150+ capitula) remains untranslated - only Thaner's Latin edition (Innsbruck, 1915) and manuscript facsimiles (Parker Library) exist; Kathleen Cushing's Papacy and Law in the Gregorian Revolution (Oxford, 1998) is an English study of it, not a translation. However, passages from the Liber contra Wibertum are translated in English in Robinson 2004 (per the storicamente.org article on Matilda of Tuscany and Anselm of Lucca, citing 'translation of passages from Anselm II of Lucca's Liber contra Wibertum in Robinson 2004'). Bulk stands untranslated.

name: Thiofridus Efternacensis
evidence: 3 searches found no English translation of the Flores epytaphii sanctorum (critical edition: Michele Camillo Ferrari, Brepols/CCCM, 1996, Latin) or the Vita Willibrordi (German translation exists: Reischmann, 1989; English none). English-language scholarship engages the treatise (Visser's 2018 Utrecht PhD thesis 'Parallel Lives'; Wieland on Thiofrid's hermeneutic style) but no translation located.

name: Usuardus Sangermanensis
evidence: 3 searches found no English translation of Usuard's Martyrologium (c. 875, ~1100 notices). Editions are Latin: PL 123-124 and J. Dubois's critical edition from Paris BnF lat. 13745. Facsimile editions (Moleiro, 1997) have Spanish commentary. The Old English Martyrology (translated by Rauer) is a different, earlier text; the modern Roman Martyrology in English is a descendant, not a translation of Usuard.

name: Joannes Venetus
evidence: 3 searches confirm no published English (or French or other international) translation of John the Deacon's Istoria Veneticorum exists - stated explicitly by History Walks in Venice's source survey. Critical edition with Italian translation: Luigi Andrea Berto (1999). Berto's English-language volume (The Political and Social Vocabulary of John the Deacon's 'Istoria Veneticorum', trans. Shugaar, Brepols 2013) is an analytical study, not a translation of the chronicle. A short translated excerpt ('The settlements of the lagoons') appears on the History Walks in Venice website, but no published translation.

name: Aimoinus Sangermanensis
evidence: 3 searches plus a verification WebFetch found no English translation. Note the claim conflates two Aimoins: Aimoin of Saint-Germain-des-Prés (9th c.: De miraculis sancti Germani, De Normanorum gestis, Translatio Sancti Vincentii - the PL 126 author) and Aimoin of Fleury (c. 960-1010: Historia/Gesta Francorum Libri V, Vita Abbonis). Neither is translated: Fleury's Historia Francorum exists in MGH Latin (ed. Waitz); the Vita Abbonis in Bautier-Labory's edition; the Saint-Germain works were edited in Historiae Francorum Scriptores (Paris, 1639-49). Fetched the Wikipedia article on Aimoin of Saint-Germain to verify: no English translation is mentioned (a claimed 'Bullough' translation surfaced in one search summary but could not be verified on the page).
